assessments.reasoning: Printed I-28 §3.5.1 places the postconditional immediately after the eligible command word. It exempts ELSE, FOR and IF, allows the command to execute when the expression is absent or true, and passes over the command and arguments when false.

challenge.method: Test a false command-level condition against a true or absent condition and the three excluded commands. Distinguish a DO, GOTO or XECUTE argument postconditional from the command-level form. Check the next-section discussion of significant spaces.
challenge.results: A false command-level condition prevents execution and argument processing. A true or absent condition permits normal command handling. The argument-level constructs are described separately and the placement immediately after the command is part of the cited rule.

limitations: The statement describes the historical whole-command form. It supplies no additional rule about a vendor’s later command set, treatment of unrelated commands or argument-level evaluation.
